column1: Inconsistent page titles displayed across multiple navigation menu items
column26:
Several navigation menu items display page titles that do not match the selected menu item name, causing inconsistency in the user interface and potentially confusing users.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Open the application.
# Navigate through the left-side menu items.
# Observe the page title displayed after selecting each menu item.

*Actual Result:*
The displayed page titles differ from the corresponding menu item names.

*Examples:*

* Menu Item: "Inputs" → Displayed Title: "Input field"
* Menu Item: "Checkbox" → Displayed Title: "Checkboxes"
* Menu Item: "Select" → Displayed Title: "Select inputs"
* Menu Item: “New tab” → Displayed Title: “Open link in a new tab”
* Menu Item: “Text area” → Displayed Title: “TextArea inputs”
* Menu Item: “Drag and Drop” → Displayed Title: “Drag-n-drop”

*Expected Result:*
The page title should match the selected navigation menu item name or follow a consistent naming convention throughout the application.

*Severity:* Low

*Priority:* Low

* At least one uppercase letter is required.
* At least one lowercase letter is required.
* At least one digit is required.
* At least one special character is required.

column1: Generic error message is displayed when password validation requirements are not met
column26:
The application displays a generic error message ("Low password complexity") when the entered password does not satisfy one or more password requirements. The error message does not clearly indicate which validation rule has failed, making it difficult for users to understand how to correct their input.

*Preconditions:*
User is on the Password Validation page/form.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Open the Password Validation form.
# Enter a password that violates one or more password requirements (e.g., "password" - no uppercase letter, digit, or special character).
# Submit the form.

*Actual Result:*
The application displays the message:
"Low password complexity"

*Expected Result:*
The application should display a clear validation message indicating which password requirement(s) are not met, for example:

* Password must contain at least 8 characters.
* Password must contain at least one uppercase letter.
* Password must contain at least one lowercase letter.
* Password must contain at least one digit.
* Password must contain at least one special character.

Alternatively, the application should provide specific feedback for each failed validation rule.

*Severity:* Medium

*Priority:* Medium

*Environment:*

* Browser:Chrome Browser
* Version: 152.0.7977.83

column26:
*Bug Type:* Functional

column1: Bottom square can be dragged multiple times if not dropped onto the top square
column26:
*Component:* Drag and Drop – Boxes page
*URL:* [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|smart-link] 

*Priority:* Medium
*Severity:* Minor (functional, not blocking, but violates stated requirement)

*Environment:* [fill in browser/OS you tested on, e.g. Chrome 128 / Windows 11]

*Requirement violated:*
"The bottom square can only be dragged once"

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Go to [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|smart-link] 
# Drag the bottom square ("Drag me") to any location that is *not* the top square ("Drop here")
# Release the mouse — the square stays where dropped
# Repeat step 2–3 multiple times, dragging the square to different empty areas
# Observe how many times the drag can be repeated

*Expected Result:*
Per the stated requirement, the bottom square should only be draggable once — implying that after the first drag (or first drag attempt), further dragging should be disabled or ignored, regardless of where it lands.

*Actual Result:*
The square can be dragged an unlimited number of times, as long as it is not dropped onto the top square. The "once only" restriction is only enforced once the square is successfully dropped on the top square (triggering "Dropped!"), not on the act of dragging itself.

*Additional Notes:*
This suggests the "drag count" or "locked" state is being set only inside the successful-drop event handler, rather than on drag start/end in general. If the intent was "the user gets one shot at placing it," the fix should track drag attempts (or lock the element after the first drag interaction) rather than only locking on successful drop.

column1: Double-clicking the smiley moves it between squares without updating "Dropped!" text, leaving text behind in the wrong square
column26:
*Component:* Drag and Drop – Images page
*URL:* [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|smart-link] 

*Priority:* High
*Severity:* Major

*Environment:* Chrome Browser / Windows 11

*Requirement violated:*
"When dropping the smiley into any of the squares, the text 'Dropped!' should appear in this square" (and, as a side effect, "A square without a smiley must be completely empty")

*Preconditions:* The smiley has already been dropped into a square at least once (so "Dropped!" is showing).

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Go to [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|smart-link] 
# Drag the smiley into a square; confirm "Dropped!" appears there correctly
# Double-click the smiley (see attachments).
# Observe the smiley's position and the "Dropped!" text's position
# Repeat drag + double-click a few times

*Expected Result:*
Either double-click has no effect, or if it moves the smiley, "Dropped!" text moves with it to the correct square.

*Actual Result:*
Double-clicking moves the smiley to the other square, but "Dropped!" text stays behind in the square the smiley left. Repeating the action causes the text to keep lagging one square behind the smiley's actual position — resulting in a square showing "Dropped!" with no smiley present.

*Additional Notes:* Suggests double-click is bound to a separate handler that moves the element without triggering the same drop-state update as the drag-and-drop flow. Worth a quick check on other click interactions too.

*Related issues:* See MFW-51 — same page/feature, different root cause.
